sequence_description: Direct JWT endpoint: attempt alg=none unsigned JWT acceptance vs a valid signed control JWT under the same role.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_alg_none_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_alg_none_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Vault accepted an unsigned JWT (alg=none); proof authenticity was not enforced on the consumed token.

sequence_description: Direct JWT endpoint: demonstrate control acceptance with trusted key, then rotate trust anchor and attempt login with a JWT signed by the previously-trusted key (should be rejected).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_oldkey_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_oldkey_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Vault accepted a JWT signed by a key that should no longer be trusted after rotation; verification policy may not match consumed proof.

sequence_description: I1 kid-injection/key-confusion probe: configure static trusted pubkeys, then attempt login with a JWT that advertises a malicious kid and is signed by an untrusted key. Secure behavior: reject. If accepted, verification may be using attacker-selected key material rather than configured trust.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_kid_injection_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_kid_injection_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Vault accepted an attacker-signed JWT by honoring attacker-controlled kid/key selection rather than configured jwt_validation_pubkeys.

sequence_description: JWT trust anchor rotation: accept key-A baseline, rotate to key-B, then ensure key-A-signed JWT is rejected on new login (no stale JWKS/pubkey cache).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attack_old_keyA_after_rotation_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attack_old_keyA_after_rotation_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Login with old key-A succeeded after trust rotated to key-B (stale trust anchor / non-atomic validation).

sequence_description: I4 case_confusion: two upstream principals differ only by case in sub ('Admin' vs 'admin'). Secure behavior: they must map to different Vault entities; if Vault normalizes case, identities may collapse.
